html:
SMTO-GWT-0082 — Confirmation Required

GUID: e54ca0ab-20ce-56bc-8620-0059146452e2
Slug: gpu-confirmation-required
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO stopped a request to reset a graphics card (GPU) because you had not approved that exact reset. The GPU was not reset.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO again to reset the GPU, naming the same computer and the same graphics card. A fresh request lets SMTO ask for your approval of this one reset.
  2. When the Unsafe action requires confirmation window appears, check the Target and Exact operation, then select Proceed. SMTO resets a GPU only with your approval for that exact card and action; an old or expired approval does not count.
  3. Before you approve, close or finish any programs that are using that graphics card. A reset interrupts everything running on the card, and SMTO will not close those programs for you.

What success looks like

  • After you select Proceed, the Task continues and reports that the GPU reset finished.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer's Gateway. Don't force a reset some other way while programs may still be using the card.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway GPU service refused a GPU reset because the request carried no current unsafe-action authorization (reset_authorized was false), so it stopped before touching the device.

What this means

  • Reset admission found reset_authorized false and refused the operation before device configuration. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Reset admission found reset_authorized false and refused the operation before device configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current unsafe-action policy and authorization bound to the selected UUID and operation.

How to fix it

  • GpuService._configure rejects operation 'reset' unless GpuRequest.reset_authorized is true, which GatewayClient sets only when the execution context's _authorized_unsafe_action.action is 'gpu_reset'. Re-request the reset so the unsafe-action confirmation flow binds owner approval to that exact GPU UUID and operation; never set the flag from tool arguments, kill GPU clients automatically or replay an uncertain reset.
  • Use the normal unsafe-action confirmation policy for the exact UUID and operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the normal unsafe-action confirmation policy for the exact UUID and operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The normal policy supplies current authority for that exact reset and all device safety prerequisites still pass.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
